hook: 72 qubits simulate 2D Fermi‑Hubbard dynamics — plus 4 more

items.claim: Programmable digital quantum simulation of 2D Fermi‑Hubbard dynamics using 72 superconducting qubits
First experimental demonstration of natural hovering extremum seeking in flapping flight
items.attribution: Elgohary and Eisa, Physical Review E (2025)

items.claim: Caltech chip steers light with another beam in 74 femtoseconds
Long‑legged direct‑drive monopedal robot achieves exceptional jump height
Dr‑LiSA aligns radar and lidar scans for SE(3) localization directly

caption: From quantum simulators to bio‑inspired robots, this week’s breakthroughs push the limits of speed and agility. Which of these advances will reshape your tech landscape next?
alt_text: Five slides on flat colour backgrounds: slide 1 states a 72‑qubit quantum simulation of 2D Fermi‑Hubbard dynamics; slide 2 announces the first natural hovering extremum seeking flapping‑flight experiment; slide 3 reports a Caltech chip steering light in 74 femtoseconds; slide 4 describes a long‑legged direct‑drive monopedal robot achieving record jump height; slide 5 notes Dr‑LiSA aligning radar and lidar scans for SE(3) localization.
